title: Fingerprint Analysis
summary: How friction-ridge impressions are developed, preserved, compared and reported — including partial prints, distortion and uncertainty.
workflow: Document the scene and collection context
Develop and preserve impressions using validated methods
Compare ridge detail and assess quality
limits: A partial or distorted impression may not support a reliable conclusion. A visual resemblance is not an identification.

title: DNA Profiling
summary: An introduction to sample collection, STR profiling, mixtures, contamination risks and statistical interpretation.
workflow: Document collection and chain of custody
limits: A DNA association does not establish when, how or why biological material was deposited.

title: Digital Forensics
summary: Forensic acquisition, file systems, logs, metadata, deleted data and preserving original digital media.
limits: Device timestamps can be affected by settings, time zones, synchronisation and system behaviour.

title: Forensic Toxicology
summary: How laboratories detect and interpret drugs, alcohol and toxic substances in biological specimens.
workflow: Interpret results with medical and case context
limits: Detection alone does not establish impairment, cause of death or timing without context.

title: Firearms & Toolmarks
summary: The basics of firearm evidence, cartridge cases, projectiles, toolmarks and trajectory reconstruction.
limits: Conclusions must not claim a unique source beyond what the method and evidence support.

title: Questioned Documents
summary: Paper and ink characteristics, alterations, printing processes, indented writing and handwriting comparison.
limits: Handwriting opinions are comparative assessments and should not be presented as infallible identification.

title: Bloodstain Pattern Analysis
summary: An overview of documenting bloodstain patterns, evaluating competing explanations and communicating uncertainty.
workflow: Photograph and map stains before collection
Record stain shape, distribution and substrate
limits: Patterns can be altered by movement, cleaning, surface texture and other factors; avoid overconfident reconstruction.

title: Forensic Anthropology
summary: How specialists assess skeletal remains to support biological profile estimation, trauma analysis and identification efforts.
workflow: Compare with missing-person and identification data
limits: Estimates are probabilistic and should not be mistaken for exact identity without corroboration.
